author: Bay State News
title: Patriots prepare for 2026 NFL Draft with top 50 prospects list
text:
The New England Patriots released their annual Big Board of draft prospects on Apr. 14, outlining the top 50 players who could fit with the team in the upcoming 2026 National Football League Draft.
This year marks a shift for the Patriots, who hold the thirty-first overall pick after reaching Super Bowl LX. The team had previously picked in the top four for two consecutive years but now faces uncertainty about which positions will be available late in the first round and whether to consider trading up or down.
According to the Big Board, wide receiver Denzel Boston from Washington is a standout prospect despite not running a timed sprint this spring. Edge rusher Cashius Howell and offensive tackle Blake Miller are also among those highlighted as potential fits at key positions such as edge, wide receiver, and tackle. Defensive line depth is noted as an area that could be addressed if highly ranked players like Kayden McDonald from Ohio State become available at pick thirty-one.
The board emphasizes that later rounds will play an important role in shaping this year’s draft class for New England due to deep talent pools at several positions. Players such as Max Iheanachor (offensive tackle), Anthony Hill Jr. (linebacker), and A.J. Haulcy (safety) are mentioned among others who may contribute beyond day one of selections.
This release represents year sixteen of what has become an annual tradition for Patriots coverage, offering fans insight into possible draft scenarios and needs across both offense and defense. The full list covers a range of roles including defensive linemen, linebackers, safeties, tight ends, receivers, tackles, guards, corners, running backs and edge rushers.
